chapter_text:
CHAPTER 21 — तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते (TEJASAM HI NA VAYAH SAMIKSHYATE)

Introduction — पाठपरिचयः

The title of this lesson is the final quarter (पादः) of a celebrated verse from महाकविः कालिदासः's epic रघुवंशम् (Raghuvamsha): तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते — 'for of the brilliant, age is not considered.' The word तेजस् means inner fire, lustre, brilliance — the light of talent, courage, learning and character that shines out of a person. वयस् means age. The poet's point is simple and bold: when a person carries real तेजस्, we do not stop to count his or her years before giving respect or responsibility. Merit, not the calendar, is the true measure of a person. In this lesson we study the verse in its story-context, read a simple Sanskrit narrative about the boy रामः and the sage विश्वामित्रः, meet more shining young achievers of the Sanskrit tradition — अष्टावक्रः, the young prince रघुः and आचार्यः शङ्करः — learn supporting public-domain verses from मनुस्मृतिः, भवभूतिः and हितोपदेशः with their शब्दार्थ, and finally draw grammar (सन्धिः, विभक्तिः, शब्दरूपम्, धातुरूपम्) from what we have read.

The verse and its context — मूलश्लोकः

कौशिकेन स किल क्षितीश्वरो राममध्वरविघातशान्तये ।
काकपक्षधरमेत्य याचितस्तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते ॥ (रघुवंशम्)

शब्दार्थ: कौशिकेन = by Kaushika, i.e. the sage विश्वामित्रः (born in the Kushika family); सः = that; किल = indeed, as tradition tells; क्षितीश्वरः = the lord of the earth, the king (दशरथः; क्षिति = earth, ईश्वरः = lord); रामम् = (for) Rama; अध्वरविघातशान्तये = for quelling the disruption of the sacrifice (अध्वरः = sacrifice, यज्ञः; विघातः = obstruction, disruption; शान्तये = for the quelling, चतुर्थी 'for'); काकपक्षधरम् = wearing the काकपक्ष, the side-locks of hair worn by boys — i.e. still a mere boy; एत्य = having approached; याचितः = was asked, was begged; तेजसाम् = of the brilliant, of those who possess तेजस्; हि = for, indeed; न = not; वयः = age; समीक्ष्यते = is considered, is looked at.

Translation: Kaushika (Vishvamitra), having approached, asked that king (Dasharatha) for Rama — a boy still wearing the side-locks of childhood — in order to quell the disruption of his sacrifice; for of the brilliant, age is not considered.

Context: The sage विश्वामित्रः was performing a great यज्ञ in the forest, but the demons मारीचः and सुबाहुः, with the terrible demoness ताटका, kept polluting and disrupting it. The sage came to अयोध्या and asked King दशरथः to send his eldest son रामः — then only a boy — to protect the sacrifice. The king trembled: how could a child face demons whom even warriors feared? But the family preceptor वसिष्ठः reminded him of Rama's extraordinary तेजस्, and Dasharatha yielded. Kalidasa seals the moment with the immortal reason: तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते. The sage did not weigh Rama's years; he saw Rama's fire.

सरला कथा — विश्वामित्रः रामं याचते (A simple Sanskrit story)

अयोध्यायां दशरथः नाम नृपः आसीत्। तस्य ज्येष्ठः पुत्रः रामः तदा बालः एव आसीत्। एकदा महर्षिः विश्वामित्रः राजसभाम् आगच्छत्। सः अवदत् — 'हे राजन्! मम यज्ञं राक्षसाः विघ्नन्ति। तस्य रक्षणाय तव पुत्रं रामं देहि' इति। राजा अचिन्तयत् — 'रामः बालः अस्ति। कथं सः राक्षसान् जेष्यति?' इति। परन्तु गुरोः वसिष्ठस्य वचनेन सः रामं लक्ष्मणं च मुनये अयच्छत्। बालः रामः ताटकां अवधीत्, मुनेः यज्ञं च अरक्षत्। सत्यम् एव उक्तम् — तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते।

शब्दार्थ: नृपः = king; ज्येष्ठः = eldest; राजसभाम् = to the royal court; विघ्नन्ति = (they) obstruct; रक्षणाय = for the protection; देहि = give; अचिन्तयत् = thought; जेष्यति = will conquer; गुरोः वचनेन = by the word of the guru; मुनये = to the sage; अयच्छत् = gave; अवधीत् = slew; अरक्षत् = protected.

Translation: In Ayodhya there was a king named Dasharatha. His eldest son Rama was then only a boy. One day the great sage Vishvamitra came to the royal court. He said, 'O king! Demons are disrupting my sacrifice. Give me your son Rama for its protection.' The king thought, 'Rama is a boy. How will he conquer the demons?' But at the word of the guru Vasishtha he gave Rama and Lakshmana to the sage. The boy Rama slew Tataka and protected the sage's sacrifice. Truly it is said — of the brilliant, age is not considered.

Moral: Responsibility should be given to ability, not to age. The boy who has prepared himself can do what grown men fear.

More young achievers — अन्ये तेजस्विनः बालाः

1) अष्टावक्रः — the eight-bend sage. अष्टावक्रः द्वादशवर्षीयः बालः आसीत्। तस्य शरीरम् अष्टसु स्थानेषु वक्रम् आसीत्, अतः सः 'अष्टावक्रः' इति नाम अलभत। तस्य पिता कहोडः जनकस्य सभायां बन्दिना वादे पराजितः आसीत्। बालः अष्टावक्रः जनकस्य सभाम् अगच्छत्। सभासदः तस्य वक्रं शरीरं दृष्ट्वा अहसन्। बालः अवदत् — 'यूयं चर्म एव पश्यथ, ज्ञानं न पश्यथ' इति। ततः सः बन्दिनं वादे अजयत्, पितरं च अमोचयत्। (Ashtavakra was a twelve-year-old boy whose body was bent in eight places — hence his name. His father Kahoda had been defeated in debate by Bandin at King Janaka's court. The boy Ashtavakra went to Janaka's assembly. The courtiers laughed on seeing his crooked body. The boy said, 'You see only the skin; you do not see knowledge.' Then he defeated Bandin in debate and freed his father.) The story, told in the महाभारतम् (वनपर्व), teaches that wisdom is measured neither by the body's shape nor by the number of years.

2) रघुः — the boy who fought Indra. In रघुवंशम् (sarga 3), Kalidasa tells how young prince रघुः, son of King दिलीपः, was set to guard the sacrificial horse of his father's अश्वमेध. When इन्द्रः himself invisibly carried the horse away, the young prince pursued the king of the gods and fought him fearlessly. Indra, delighted by the boy's तेजस्, granted his father the fruit of the sacrifice. The dynasty itself came to be called after this brilliant youth — रघुवंशः.

3) शङ्करः — the boy philosopher. Tradition remembers आदिशङ्कराचार्यः with this verse: अष्टवर्षे चतुर्वेदी द्वादशे सर्वशास्त्रवित् । षोडशे कृतवान् भाष्यं द्वात्रिंशे मुनिरभ्यगात् ॥ — 'At eight a master of the four Vedas, at twelve a knower of all shastras, at sixteen he composed his commentaries (भाष्य on the उपनिषद्, गीता and ब्रह्मसूत्र), and at thirty-two the sage departed.' A boy-sannyasi walked the length of India and debated its greatest scholars — and won. Age did not limit his तेजस्.

Supporting verses — अन्ये श्लोकाः

(1) न तेन वृद्धो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः ।
यो वै युवाप्यधीयानस्तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः ॥ (मनुस्मृतिः)
शब्दार्थ: तेन = by that; वृद्धः = old, venerable; भवति = becomes; येन = by which; अस्य = his; पलितम् = grey; शिरः = head; यः = who; वै = indeed; युवा = young; अपि = even; अधीयानः = studying, learned; तम् = him; देवाः = the gods; स्थविरम् = elder, venerable; विदुः = know, regard.
Translation: One does not become venerable merely because his head is grey; the one who, though young, is learned — him the gods regard as an elder.
Moral: True seniority is of knowledge, not of hair. The verse is the perfect companion of Kalidasa's line.

(2) गुणाः पूजास्थानं गुणिषु न च लिङ्गं न च वयः । (भवभूतिः, उत्तररामचरितम्)
शब्दार्थ: गुणाः = qualities, merits; पूजास्थानम् = the ground/place of honour; गुणिषु = in the virtuous, in those who possess merits; लिङ्गम् = outward mark (sex, dress, form); वयः = age.
Translation: In the virtuous, it is qualities that are the ground of honour — neither outward form nor age.
Moral: Bhavabhuti states as a rule what Kalidasa showed in story: we honour गुण, not appearance or years.

(3) काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम् ।
व्यसनेन च मूर्खाणां निद्रया कलहेन वा ॥ (हितोपदेशः)
शब्दार्थ: काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन = in the delight of poetry and learning; कालः = time; गच्छति = goes, passes; धीमताम् = of the wise; व्यसनेन = in vice/addiction; मूर्खाणाम् = of the foolish; निद्रया = in sleep; कलहेन = in quarrel; वा = or.
Translation: The time of the wise passes in the delight of poetry and learning; that of fools in vice, sleep or quarrel.
Moral: तेजस् is not an accident of birth alone — it is kindled by the right use of time. The young who spend their hours in study become the तेजस्विन् whom age cannot measure.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the verses

(A) सन्धिः (Sandhi). Examples drawn from this lesson:
  • येन + अस्य → येनास्य (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धिः) — split it back as येन + अस्य.
  • युवा + अपि → युवापि (आ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धिः); then अपि + अधीयानः → अप्यधीयानः (इ + अ → य्, यण्-सन्धिः). So युवाप्यधीयानः = युवा + अपि + अधीयानः.
  • च + एव → चैव (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धि-सन्धिः).
  • याचितः + तेजसाम् → याचितस्तेजसाम् (the विसर्ग ः before त् becomes स् — विसर्ग-सन्धिः).
  • काकपक्षधरम् + एत्य → काकपक्षधरमेत्य (म् joins the following vowel).
Being able to split a joined form (सन्धि-विच्छेदः) is a key reading skill.

(B) विभक्तिः (Case endings), with examples from the verse and story:
  • प्रथमा (subject): रामः, नृपः, बालः, वयः (neuter subject of समीक्ष्यते).
  • द्वितीया (object): रामम् ('asked FOR Rama'), ताटकाम्, यज्ञम्, राजसभाम्.
  • तृतीया (by/with): कौशिकेन 'BY Kaushika', वचनेन 'by the word', निद्रया 'in/by sleep'.
  • चतुर्थी (for/to): शान्तये 'FOR the quelling', रक्षणाय 'for the protection', मुनये 'TO the sage'.
  • षष्ठी (of): तेजसाम् 'OF the brilliant' (plural), धीमताम् 'of the wise', मूर्खाणाम् 'of the fools', गुरोः 'of the guru'.
  • सप्तमी (in/among): गुणिषु 'among the virtuous', सभायाम् 'in the court', अष्टसु स्थानेषु 'in eight places'.

(C) शब्दरूपम् — the neuter s-stem. तेजस्, वयस्, शिरस्, मनस् are neuter nouns ending in स्. In प्रथमा: एकवचन तेजः, द्विवचन तेजसी, बहुवचन तेजांसि. So the षष्ठी बहुवचन in our title is तेजसाम् 'of the brilliant ones'. Likewise शिरः 'head' (पलितं शिरः) and वयः 'age' are प्रथमा एकवचन forms of शिरस् and वयस्.

(D) धातुरूपम् — verbs. समीक्ष्यते is the passive (कर्मवाचि) of सम् + ईक्ष् 'to look at, consider': 'is considered'. In the active we would say 'लोकः वयः न समीक्षते' (people do not consider age). Other verbs met here: भवति (भू, 'becomes'), गच्छति (गम्, 'goes'), ददाति/देहि (दा, 'gives/give!'), विदुः (विद्, 'they know'), अवदत् (वद्, past 'said'), अवधीत् (हन्/वध्, past 'slew'), अरक्षत् (रक्ष्, past 'protected').

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you studied Kalidasa's famous declaration तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते — 'of the brilliant, age is not considered' — in its context in रघुवंशम्: sage Vishvamitra asking King Dasharatha for the boy Rama, still in his काकपक्ष side-locks, to protect his sacrifice. You read a simple Sanskrit story of that episode, and met other young achievers: अष्टावक्रः, who taught Janaka's laughing courtiers that they saw only skin and not knowledge; young रघुः, who fought Indra himself; and शङ्करः, master of the Vedas at eight and commentator at sixteen. Supporting verses deepened the theme: मनुस्मृतिः (न तेन वृद्धो भवति...) says grey hair does not make an elder — learning does; भवभूतिः says qualities, not form or age, are the ground of honour; and हितोपदेशः reminds us that the wise build their brilliance by spending time in study. From the verses you drew grammar: दीर्घ, यण्, वृद्धि and विसर्ग sandhis with their splits; the seven cases through words like कौशिकेन, शान्तये, तेजसाम् and गुणिषु; the neuter s-stem declension (तेजः / तेजसी / तेजांसि); and the passive verb समीक्ष्यते. Carry the lesson with you: respect elders always, but never let anyone — including yourself — dismiss real merit merely because it is young.

topics.description: Kalidasa's line from रघुवंशम् — 'of the brilliant, age is not considered' — studied with its full verse (कौशिकेन स किल क्षितीश्वरो...), its शब्दार्थ, and its story-context: Vishvamitra asking Dasharatha for the boy Rama to protect his sacrifice.

topics.name: Young Achievers in Sanskrit Tradition
topics.description: Stories of brilliant youngsters: the boy Rama slaying Tataka, अष्टावक्रः defeating Bandin in Janaka's court, young prince रघुः fighting Indra, and the boy philosopher शङ्करः — each showing merit shining regardless of age.

topics.name: Merit over Age — Moral and Ethical Themes
topics.description: The chapter's central value: ability, learning and character — not years — are the true measure of a person; how to honour young talent while still respecting elders, and how brilliance is built by the right use of time.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Verses
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the lesson: दीर्घ, यण्, वृद्धि and विसर्ग सन्धि with सन्धि-विच्छेद; विभक्ति roles of words like कौशिकेन, शान्तये, तेजसाम्, गुणिषु; the neuter s-stem शब्दरूप (तेजः/तेजसी/तेजांसि); and the passive verb समीक्ष्यते.

sections.heading: The verse and its story
bullets: The chapter title is the last quarter of a verse of Kalidasa's रघुवंशम्: कौशिकेन स किल क्षितीश्वरो राममध्वरविघातशान्तये । काकपक्षधरमेत्य याचितस्तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते ॥
Sage Vishvamitra (कौशिकः), his sacrifice disrupted by demons, approached King Dasharatha (क्षितीश्वरः) and asked for the boy Rama, still wearing the काकपक्ष side-locks of childhood.
Dasharatha hesitated at Rama's youth, but on Vasishtha's advice sent Rama and Lakshmana; the boy slew ताटका and protected the sacrifice.
Kalidasa's reason is the moral of the whole chapter: of the brilliant (तेजसाम्), age (वयः) is not considered (न समीक्ष्यते).

sections.heading: Young achievers of the tradition
bullets: अष्टावक्रः, a boy of twelve bent in eight places, was laughed at in Janaka's court; he replied that the courtiers saw only skin, not knowledge, then defeated Bandin in debate and freed his father Kahoda.
Young prince रघुः, son of Dilipa, guarded the अश्वमेध horse and fearlessly fought Indra himself (रघुवंशम्, sarga 3); the dynasty took his name.
Tradition says of शङ्करः: at eight a master of the four Vedas, at twelve of all shastras, at sixteen the author of the great भाष्यs — a boy-sannyasi who won debates across India.
Each story shows the same truth: preparation and inner fire, not years, decide what a person can do.

sections.heading: Supporting verses on merit over age
bullets: मनुस्मृतिः: न तेन वृद्धो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः — grey hair does not make one venerable; the young man who is learned, the gods regard as the elder (स्थविरः).
भवभूतिः (उत्तररामचरितम्): गुणाः पूजास्थानं गुणिषु न च लिङ्गं न च वयः — qualities alone are the ground of honour, not outward form nor age.
हितोपदेशः: काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम् — the wise pass time in poetry and learning, fools in vice, sleep and quarrel; brilliance is earned by the right use of time.

sections.heading: Sandhi from the verses
bullets: दीर्घ-सन्धि: येन + अस्य = येनास्य (अ+अ=आ); युवा + अपि = युवापि (आ+अ=आ).
यण्-सन्धि: अपि + अधीयानः = अप्यधीयानः (इ + अ → य्); so युवाप्यधीयानः = युवा + अपि + अधीयानः.
वृद्धि-सन्धि: च + एव = चैव (अ + ए = ऐ).
विसर्ग-सन्धि: याचितः + तेजसाम् = याचितस्तेजसाम् (ः before त् becomes स्); and काकपक्षधरम् + एत्य = काकपक्षधरमेत्य.

sections.heading: Vibhakti, shabda-rupa and dhatu-rupa
bullets: तृतीया 'by': कौशिकेन, वचनेन; चतुर्थी 'for/to': शान्तये, रक्षणाय, मुनये; षष्ठी 'of': तेजसाम्, धीमताम्, मूर्खाणाम्; सप्तमी 'in/among': गुणिषु, सभायाम्.
तेजस्, वयस्, शिरस्, मनस् are neuter s-stems: प्रथमा तेजः / तेजसी / तेजांसि; hence तेजसाम् is षष्ठी बहुवचन 'of the brilliant'.
समीक्ष्यते is the passive (कर्मवाचि) of सम् + ईक्ष्: 'is considered'; other verbs of the lesson include भवति, गच्छति, विदुः, अवदत्, अवधीत्, अरक्षत्.

key_takeaways: तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते — of the brilliant, age is not considered; the line is Kalidasa's, from रघुवंशम्.
Its context: Vishvamitra asked Dasharatha for the boy Rama (काकपक्षधर) to protect his sacrifice, and the boy slew ताटका.
Ashtavakra's retort to the laughing courtiers — 'you see only skin, not knowledge' — warns us never to judge worth by appearance or age.
Manu's verse teaches that learning, not grey hair (पलितं शिरः), makes the true elder (स्थविरः).
Bhavabhuti's rule: गुणाः पूजास्थानम् — qualities alone are the ground of honour, not form or age.
Brilliance is built: the wise spend time in काव्य and शास्त्र, fools in vice, sleep and quarrel (हितोपदेशः).
Grammar: येनास्य and युवापि are दीर्घ-सन्धि, चैव is वृद्धि, याचितस्तेजसाम् is विसर्ग-सन्धि; तेजस् declines तेजः/तेजसी/तेजांसि; समीक्ष्यते is passive.

glossary.definition: Inner fire, lustre, brilliance — the light of talent, courage, learning and character; षष्ठी बहुवचन तेजसाम् 'of the brilliant'.
Age, stage of life; प्रथमा एकवचन वयः, the subject of न समीक्ष्यते in the title line.
'Is considered, is looked at' — passive (कर्मवाचि) form of सम् + ईक्ष् 'to look at, examine'.
A name of the sage विश्वामित्रः, born in the family of Kushika; the asker in Kalidasa's verse.
'Lord of the earth' (क्षिति + ईश्वरः), i.e. the king — here Dasharatha.
A sacrifice, यज्ञः; in the verse अध्वरविघातशान्तये = 'for quelling the disruption of the sacrifice'.
Obstruction, disruption — what the demons caused to Vishvamitra's sacrifice.
'Wearing the crow's-wing locks' — the side-locks of hair worn by boys; a sign that Rama was still a child.
'Was asked, was begged' — past passive participle of याच् 'to ask for'; Dasharatha was asked for Rama.
The boy sage 'bent in eight places' who defeated Bandin in Janaka's court and freed his father Kahoda (महाभारतम्, वनपर्व).
Grey (of hair); पलितं शिरः = a grey-haired head, which by itself does not make one venerable.
An elder, a venerable person; the gods regard even a learned youth as स्थविरः (मनुस्मृतिः).
One who is studying, learned; from अधि + इ 'to study' — the quality that makes the young venerable.
Quality, merit, virtue; गुणाः पूजास्थानम् — qualities are the ground of honour (भवभूतिः).
A wise, intelligent person; षष्ठी बहुवचन धीमताम् 'of the wise', whose time passes in poetry and learning.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 21)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the verses and stories in the lesson where needed.

questions.question: Name the poet and the work from which the line 'तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते' is taken, and give its English meaning.
questions.answer: The line is by महाकवि कालिदासः, from his epic रघुवंशम्. Meaning: 'For of the brilliant (those who possess तेजस्), age is not considered' — merit, not years, is the true measure of a person.
questions.explanation: Source: Kalidasa's Raghuvamsha; the line closes the verse about Vishvamitra asking for the boy Rama.

questions.question: What does काकपक्षधरम् mean, and what does it tell us about Rama in the verse?
questions.answer: काकपक्षधरम् means 'wearing the काकपक्ष' — the side-locks of hair worn by boys. It tells us that Rama was still a mere child when Vishvamitra asked for him to protect the sacrifice — which makes the poet's point about age all the stronger.
questions.explanation: The word marks Rama's boyhood; the sage still chose him, for age is not the measure of तेजस्.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: क्षितीश्वरः, अध्वरः, याचितः, एत्य.
questions.answer: क्षितीश्वरः = lord of the earth, the king (Dasharatha); अध्वरः = sacrifice (यज्ञः); याचितः = was asked/begged; एत्य = having approached.
questions.explanation: All four words come from the मूलश्लोक of the chapter.

questions.question: Write the meaning of the verse 'न तेन वृद्धो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः । यो वै युवाप्यधीयानस्तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः ॥' and state its source.
questions.answer: Source: मनुस्मृतिः. Meaning: One does not become old/venerable merely because his head has turned grey; the one who, though young, is learned (अधीयानः) — him the gods regard as the true elder (स्थविरः). Learning, not years or grey hair, makes a person worthy of the elder's seat.
questions.explanation: The Manu verse is the chapter's strongest supporting statement of merit over age.

questions.question: Why did the courtiers laugh at Ashtavakra, and what was his reply?
questions.answer: The courtiers laughed because the twelve-year-old boy's body was bent (वक्र) in eight places. Ashtavakra replied that they were seeing only the skin (चर्म) and not the knowledge (ज्ञानम्) — judging the container, not the contents. He then defeated Bandin in debate.
questions.explanation: The episode warns against judging worth by appearance or age.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) येनास्य (b) युवापि (c) चैव.
questions.answer: (a) येनास्य = येन + अस्य (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धिः). (b) युवापि = युवा + अपि (आ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धिः). (c) चैव = च + एव (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धि-सन्धिः).
questions.explanation: All three joined forms occur in the chapter's verses.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its meaning-role for each word: कौशिकेन, शान्तये, तेजसाम्.
questions.answer: कौशिकेन = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'BY Kaushika/Vishvamitra'. शान्तये = चतुर्थी (dative) → 'FOR the quelling'. तेजसाम् = षष्ठी बहुवचन (genitive plural) → 'OF the brilliant ones'.
questions.explanation: तृतीया shows the agent, चतुर्थी the purpose, षष्ठी possession/relation.

questions.question: Narrate, in your own words, the full context of the verse 'कौशिकेन स किल क्षितीश्वरो...' — who asked whom, for what, why there was hesitation, and how the episode ended.
questions.answer: The sage विश्वामित्रः (कौशिकः) was performing a great sacrifice in the forest, but demons — ताटका, मारीचः and सुबाहुः — kept disrupting it. He came to Ayodhya and asked King दशरथः (क्षितीश्वरः) to send his eldest son रामः to protect the yajna. Dasharatha hesitated, for Rama was still a boy wearing the काकपक्ष side-locks — how could a child face demons whom warriors feared? But the royal guru वसिष्ठः reminded the king of Rama's extraordinary तेजस्, and Dasharatha sent Rama with Lakshmana. The boy slew the demoness ताटका, drove off the demons and protected the sacrifice. Kalidasa closes the moment with the reason for the sage's confidence: तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते — of the brilliant, age is not considered.
questions.explanation: Full-context narration: the asker (Vishvamitra), the asked (Dasharatha), the purpose (protection of the sacrifice), the hesitation (Rama's youth) and the outcome (Tataka slain, yajna protected).

questions.question: 'तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते' — discuss this maxim with reference to today's world. Give at least two modern examples of young achievers, and explain how the maxim can be balanced with respect for elders.
questions.answer:
The maxim says that when true brilliance (तेजस्) is present, age should not be the deciding measure. Today we see it constantly: teenage chess grandmasters and Olympic medallists compete with and defeat far older champions; young scientists, coders and entrepreneurs create inventions and companies that change the world; a school student may explain new technology better than adults around her. Institutions that select by ability — not by seniority alone — find and grow such talent, exactly as Vishvamitra did with Rama.
Balance with respect for elders: the maxim does not teach disrespect. Elders carry experience, and the same tradition (मनुस्मृतिः) that honours the learned youth also teaches humility (विनयः). The right balance is: honour elders for their experience and character; honour the young for proven merit; and never dismiss either — the old as 'outdated' or the young as 'too small'. Worth, wherever it appears, deserves recognition.
questions.explanation: Expect: correct meaning, two or more modern examples, and an explicit balancing of merit-recognition with respect for elders.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'बालः रामः ताटकां अवधीत्, मुनेः यज्ञं च अरक्षत्।'
questions.answer: The boy Rama slew Tataka and protected the sage's sacrifice. (बालः रामः = the boy Rama; ताटकाम् अवधीत् = slew Tataka; मुनेः यज्ञम् = the sage's sacrifice; अरक्षत् = protected.)
questions.explanation: Simple past-tense sentence from the chapter's Sanskrit story.

questions.question: 'तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते' इति पङ्क्तिः कस्मात् ग्रन्थात् अस्ति? (From which work is this line taken?)
questions.explanation: The line closes a verse of Kalidasa's epic रघुवंशम्, in the episode of Vishvamitra asking for the boy Rama.

questions.question: रघुवंशम् इति महाकाव्यस्य कविः कः? (Who is the poet of the Raghuvamsha?)
questions.explanation: रघुवंशम् is one of the two great epics (महाकाव्य) of Kalidasa, the other being कुमारसम्भवम्.

questions.question: What is the correct meaning of 'तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते'?
options: For the brilliant, age is not considered
Youth is a great obstacle to success
questions.answer: For the brilliant, age is not considered
questions.explanation: तेजसाम् = of the brilliant; वयः = age; न समीक्ष्यते = is not considered/examined.

questions.question: श्लोके 'कौशिकः' इति पदं कं सूचयति? (In the verse, whom does 'Kaushika' refer to?)
questions.explanation: Vishvamitra, born in the family of Kushika, is called कौशिकः.

questions.question: 'क्षितीश्वरः' in the verse means
questions.explanation: क्षिति = earth, ईश्वरः = lord; 'lord of the earth' = the king, here Dasharatha.

questions.question: विश्वामित्रः रामं किमर्थम् अयाचत? (For what purpose did Vishvamitra ask for Rama?)
options: वनगमनाय (to send him to the forest)
questions.explanation: Demons were disrupting the sage's यज्ञ (अध्वर); he asked for Rama to quell the disruption (अध्वरविघातशान्तये).

questions.question: The word 'काकपक्षधरम्' tells us that Rama was
options: an old man with grey hair
questions.explanation: काकपक्ष = the 'crow's-wing' side-locks worn by boys; धरम् = wearing. Rama was still a child.

questions.question: दशरथः किमर्थं शङ्कितः आसीत्? (Why did Dasharatha hesitate?)
options: रामः बालः आसीत् (Rama was very young)
रामः वनम् अगच्छत् (Rama had gone to the forest)
मुनिः क्रुद्धः आसीत् (the sage was angry)
questions.answer: रामः बालः आसीत् (Rama was very young)
questions.explanation: The king feared sending a mere boy against demons whom even warriors feared.

questions.question: यज्ञरक्षणसमये बालः रामः कां राक्षसीम् अवधीत्? (Which demoness did the boy Rama slay while protecting the sacrifice?)
questions.explanation: Rama slew the demoness Tataka and drove away Maricha and Subahu, protecting Vishvamitra's yajna.

questions.question: Grammatically, 'समीक्ष्यते' means
questions.explanation: समीक्ष्यते is the कर्मवाचि (passive) of सम् + ईक्ष् 'to look at, consider' — age 'is not considered'.

questions.question: 'अध्वरः' इत्यस्य पदस्य अर्थः कः? (What is the meaning of the word 'adhvara'?)
questions.explanation: अध्वरः is a Vedic word for sacrifice; अध्वरविघातशान्तये = 'for quelling the disruption of the sacrifice'.

questions.question: In 'तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते', the word 'हि' means
questions.explanation: हि is an emphatic particle giving the reason: 'FOR, of the brilliant, age is not considered'.

questions.question: 'न तेन वृद्धो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः' इति श्लोकः कस्मात् ग्रन्थात्? (From which text is this verse?)
questions.explanation: The verse on grey hair versus learning comes from the मनुस्मृतिः (it also appears in the महाभारतम्).

questions.question: Complete the verse: 'यो वै युवाप्यधीयानस्तं देवाः ____ विदुः।'
questions.explanation: The gods regard the learned youth as स्थविरः — the true elder.

questions.question: 'गुणाः पूजास्थानं गुणिषु न च लिङ्गं न च वयः' — this line is by which poet?
questions.explanation: The line is from Bhavabhuti's play उत्तररामचरितम्.

questions.question: 'गुणाः पूजास्थानम्...' इति पङ्क्तिः कस्मिन् नाटके अस्ति? (In which play does this line occur?)
questions.explanation: The line is from Bhavabhuti's उत्तररामचरितम्, on the later life of Rama.

questions.question: Complete: 'काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति ____।'
questions.explanation: The time OF THE WISE (धीमताम्) passes in the delight of poetry and learning (हितोपदेशः).

questions.question: According to the same हितोपदेश verse, the time of fools passes in
options: व्यसन, निद्रा and कलह (vice, sleep and quarrel)
questions.answer: व्यसन, निद्रा and कलह (vice, sleep and quarrel)
questions.explanation: व्यसनेन च मूर्खाणां निद्रया कलहेन वा — fools waste time in vice, sleep or quarrel.

questions.question: रघुवंशम् is a work of which literary type?
questions.explanation: रघुवंशम् is a mahakavya in nineteen sargas narrating the solar dynasty of Raghu.

questions.question: रघुवंशम् describes the dynasty of
questions.explanation: The epic narrates the line of solar-dynasty kings — Dilipa, Raghu, Aja, Dasharatha, Rama and their successors.

questions.question: 'पलितं शिरः' means
questions.explanation: पलितम् = grey (of hair); शिरः = head. Grey hair alone does not make one venerable.

questions.question: 'अधीयानः' in the Manu verse means
questions.explanation: अधीयानः is from अधि + इ 'to study'; even a young man who is learned is the true elder.

questions.question: अष्टावक्रः इति नाम कथं प्राप्तम्? (How did Ashtavakra get his name?)
options: his body was bent in eight places
he knew eight branches of learning
questions.answer: his body was bent in eight places
questions.explanation: अष्ट = eight, वक्र = bent; his body was crooked in eight places from birth.

questions.question: अष्टावक्रः कस्य नृपस्य सभाम् अगच्छत्? (To whose royal court did Ashtavakra go?)
questions.explanation: He went to the court of King Janaka of Mithila, where the debate with Bandin took place.

questions.question: When Ashtavakra entered Janaka's court, the courtiers first
questions.explanation: The assembly laughed at the crooked twelve-year-old — and he answered their laughter with a lesson.

questions.question: What was Ashtavakra's reply to those who laughed at him?
options: 'You see only the skin, not the knowledge'
questions.answer: 'You see only the skin, not the knowledge'
questions.explanation: यूयं चर्म एव पश्यथ, ज्ञानं न पश्यथ — they were judging the body, not the wisdom within.

questions.question: अष्टावक्रः वादे कं पण्डितम् अजयत्? (Whom did Ashtavakra defeat in debate?)
questions.explanation: He defeated Bandin, the court scholar who had earlier defeated many brahmanas including his father.

questions.question: By winning the debate, Ashtavakra freed
questions.explanation: His father Kahoda had been defeated by Bandin; the son's victory released him.

questions.question: While guarding the sacrificial horse, young prince रघुः fought which god?
questions.explanation: In रघुवंशम् sarga 3, Indra carried off the ashvamedha horse and the young prince fearlessly fought him.

questions.question: रघुः कस्य नृपस्य पुत्रः आसीत्? (Whose son was Raghu?)
questions.explanation: Raghu was the son of King Dilipa; his own son was Aja, grandfather of Rama.

questions.question: According to tradition, शङ्करः mastered the four Vedas by the age of
questions.explanation: अष्टवर्षे चतुर्वेदी — 'at eight, a master of the four Vedas', says the traditional verse about Shankara.

questions.question: The great works composed by the young शङ्करः were
options: भाष्यs (commentaries) on the Upanishads, Gita and Brahmasutra
court epics in praise of kings
questions.answer: भाष्यs (commentaries) on the Upanishads, Gita and Brahmasutra
questions.explanation: षोडशे कृतवान् भाष्यम् — at sixteen he had composed his commentaries on the प्रस्थानत्रयी.

questions.question: The common lesson of the stories of Rama, Ashtavakra, Raghu and Shankara is
options: one must wait for old age to achieve
questions.explanation: Each was very young, and each achieved what the old could not — तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT among the young achievers discussed in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The chapter's young achievers are Rama, Ashtavakra, Raghu and Shankara; Bhishma is not discussed.

questions.question: 'तेजस्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः? (What does 'tejas' mean?)
questions.explanation: तेजस् is lustre, inner fire — the light of talent, courage and character.

questions.question: 'वयः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः? (What does 'vayah' mean?)
questions.explanation: वयः (from वयस्) means age or stage of life.

questions.question: 'याचितः' means
questions.explanation: याचितः is the past passive participle of याच् 'to ask for' — Dasharatha 'was asked' for Rama.

questions.question: 'एत्य' means
questions.explanation: एत्य = आ + इ + ल्यप्, the gerund 'having come/approached' — the sage came to the king and asked.

questions.question: 'शान्तये' means
questions.explanation: शान्तये is चतुर्थी of शान्ति — 'FOR the quelling' of the sacrifice's disruption.

questions.question: 'विघातः' means
questions.explanation: विघातः = disruption; the demons caused विघात to Vishvamitra's sacrifice.

questions.question: 'स्थविरः' means
questions.explanation: स्थविरः is the venerable elder; the gods so regard even a learned youth.

questions.question: 'देवाः विदुः' means
questions.explanation: विदुः is the plural of विद् 'to know' — 'the gods KNOW/regard him as an elder'.

questions.question: 'धीमताम्' means
questions.explanation: धीमताम् is षष्ठी बहुवचन of धीमान् 'wise' — the time OF THE WISE passes in study.

questions.question: 'निद्रया' means
questions.explanation: निद्रया is तृतीया of निद्रा 'sleep' — fools pass their time in sleep.

questions.question: 'कलहः' means
questions.explanation: कलहः = quarrel; कलहेन 'in quarrel' is one of the fool's pastimes in the हितोपदेश verse.

questions.question: 'गुणिषु' means
questions.explanation: गुणिषु is सप्तमी बहुवचन of गुणिन् 'possessing merits' — 'IN/AMONG the virtuous, qualities are the ground of honour'.

questions.question: In Bhavabhuti's line, 'लिङ्गम्' means
questions.explanation: लिङ्गम् here is the outward mark (form, dress, sex) — honour rests on गुण, not on outward form or age.

questions.question: In 'सः रामं मुनये अयच्छत्', the word 'मुनये' means
questions.explanation: मुनये is चतुर्थी of मुनि — the king gave Rama TO the sage.

questions.question: The central theme of this chapter is
options: age must be honoured above all else
fame is the goal of life
questions.explanation: All the verses and stories teach one truth: तेजस् (merit/brilliance), not वयः (age), is the true measure.

questions.question: Which situation BEST applies the maxim 'तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते'?
options: a young student is chosen to lead the science team because of her ability
the oldest student is always made the leader
the richest student is made the leader
the tallest student is made the leader
questions.answer: a young student is chosen to lead the science team because of her ability
questions.explanation: The maxim asks us to weigh merit, not age (or wealth or size), when giving responsibility.

questions.question: According to the Manu verse, one truly becomes 'वृद्ध' (venerable) through
questions.explanation: Not grey hair (पलितं शिरः) but learning makes the elder; the learned youth is स्थविरः to the gods.

questions.question: Bhavabhuti's line says the ground of honour (पूजास्थानम्) among the virtuous is
questions.explanation: गुणाः पूजास्थानं गुणिषु — qualities alone earn honour; neither form nor age.

questions.question: According to this chapter, what attitude should elders take toward talented youngsters?
options: dismiss them until they grow older
test them only by their age
questions.explanation: As Vishvamitra recognised Rama's तेजस्, elders should see and nurture ability wherever it appears.

questions.question: The हितोपदेश verse (काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन...) implies that brilliance grows chiefly from
options: the right use of time in study
questions.answer: the right use of time in study
questions.explanation: The wise spend time in काव्य and शास्त्र — that is how तेजस् is kindled and grown.

questions.question: 'Age is only the body's count; तेजस् is the soul's light.' This statement
questions.explanation: The chapter consistently values inner brilliance over the outward count of years.

questions.question: Judging Ashtavakra by his bent body was an error of
options: confusing outer form with inner worth
questions.answer: confusing outer form with inner worth
questions.explanation: The courtiers judged the 'skin'; Ashtavakra's knowledge proved that worth lies within.

questions.question: युवा + अपि = ?
questions.explanation: आ + अ = आ (दीर्घ-सन्धिः): युवा + अपि = युवापि.

questions.question: येन + अस्य = ?
questions.explanation: अ + अ = आ (दीर्घ-सन्धिः): येन + अस्य = येनास्य, as in 'येनास्य पलितं शिरः'.

questions.question: The correct सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'काकपक्षधरमेत्य' is
questions.explanation: The final म् of काकपक्षधरम् joins the vowel of एत्य 'having approached'.

questions.question: याचितः + तेजसाम् joins to give
questions.explanation: विसर्ग-सन्धिः: the visarga ः before त् becomes स् — याचितः + तेजसाम् = याचितस्तेजसाम्.

questions.question: अपि + अधीयानः = ?
questions.explanation: यण्-सन्धिः: इ + अ → य् — अपि + अधीयानः = अप्यधीयानः, as in युवाप्यधीयानः.

questions.question: च + एव = ?
questions.explanation: वृद्धि-सन्धिः: अ + ए = ऐ — च + एव = चैव.

questions.question: In दीर्घ-सन्धि, अ + अ gives
questions.explanation: Two similar short vowels merge into the corresponding long vowel: अ + अ = आ.

questions.question: 'तेजसाम्' पदे का विभक्तिः? (Which vibhakti is in 'tejasam'?)
questions.explanation: तेजसाम् = genitive plural of तेजस् — 'OF the brilliant ones'.

questions.question: 'कौशिकेन' पदे का विभक्तिः? (Which vibhakti is in 'Kaushikena'?)
questions.explanation: कौशिकेन is instrumental — the king was asked BY Kaushika.

questions.question: 'शान्तये' पदे का विभक्तिः? (Which vibhakti is in 'shantaye'?)
questions.explanation: शान्तये is dative of शान्ति — 'FOR the quelling' (purpose).

questions.question: 'गुणिषु' पदे का विभक्तिः? (Which vibhakti is in 'gunishu'?)
questions.explanation: गुणिषु = locative plural of गुणिन् — 'AMONG the virtuous'.

questions.question: The प्रथमा बहुवचन (nominative plural) of the neuter noun 'तेजस्' is
questions.explanation: Neuter s-stems decline तेजः / तेजसी / तेजांसि in the nominative.

questions.question: 'समीक्ष्यते' is in which voice (वाच्य)?
questions.explanation: समीक्ष्यते = 'is considered' — the passive of सम् + ईक्ष्; वयः is its grammatical subject.

questions.question: 'विदुः' is a form of which धातु (root)?
questions.explanation: विदुः 'they know' is the third-person plural of विद् — देवाः स्थविरं विदुः.

questions.question: The correct translation of 'बालः रामः ताटकां अवधीत्' is
questions.explanation: बालः रामः = subject; ताटकाम् = object; अवधीत् = slew (past of हन्/वध्).

questions.question: 'मम यज्ञं राक्षसाः विघ्नन्ति' means
questions.explanation: मम यज्ञम् = my sacrifice (object); राक्षसाः = demons (subject); विघ्नन्ति = obstruct.

questions.question: 'कथं सः राक्षसान् जेष्यति?' means
options: How will he conquer the demons?
Why did he fear the demons?
When did the demons conquer him?
Where will he find the demons?
questions.answer: How will he conquer the demons?
questions.explanation: कथम् = how; जेष्यति = will conquer (future of जि); राक्षसान् = the demons (object).

questions.question: The best English rendering of 'तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः' is
options: The gods regard him as an elder
The gods make him grow old
He knows the gods are old
questions.answer: The gods regard him as an elder
questions.explanation: तम् ... स्थविरम् is a double accusative with विदुः: they know/regard HIM AS an elder.

questions.question: In 'सः रामं मुनये अयच्छत्', who is the giver (कर्ता)?
questions.explanation: सः refers to the king: Dasharatha (subject) gave Rama (object) to the sage (मुनये, dative).

questions.question: The line 'तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते' occurs in Kalidasa's रघुवंशम्. (True/False)
questions.explanation: It is the closing quarter of a verse in the Raghuvamsha, in the episode of Vishvamitra asking for the boy Rama.

questions.question: In the verse, Vishvamitra asked Dasharatha for Bharata to protect his sacrifice. (True/False)
questions.explanation: He asked for रामः (with Lakshmana accompanying), not Bharata.

questions.question: According to the मनुस्मृति verse, one becomes venerable (वृद्ध) merely by having grey hair. (True/False)
questions.explanation: न तेन वृद्धो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः — grey hair does NOT make one venerable; learning does.

questions.question: Ashtavakra was laughed at in Janaka's court because of his bent body. (True/False)
questions.explanation: The courtiers laughed at his body bent in eight places; he replied that they saw only skin, not knowledge.

questions.question: Shankaracharya wrote his great commentaries only in his old age. (True/False)
questions.explanation: Tradition says he composed his भाष्यs by the age of sixteen — षोडशे कृतवान् भाष्यम्.

questions.question: 'काकपक्ष' refers to the side-locks of hair worn by boys. (True/False)
questions.explanation: काकपक्ष ('crow's wing') is the boys' side-lock hairstyle; काकपक्षधरः रामः was still a child.

questions.question: Bhavabhuti's line says that among the virtuous, qualities — not outward form or age — are the ground of honour. (True/False)
questions.explanation: गुणाः पूजास्थानं गुणिषु न च लिङ्गं न च वयः — qualities alone earn honour.

questions.question: The सन्धि of येन + अस्य is येनास्य. (True/False)
questions.explanation: अ + अ = आ (दीर्घ-सन्धिः), giving येनास्य as in the Manu verse.

questions.question: 'समीक्ष्यते' is an active-voice verb meaning 'he considers'. (True/False)
questions.explanation: समीक्ष्यते is passive (कर्मवाचि): 'is considered'. The active would be समीक्षते.

questions.question: 'काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम्' means: the time of the wise passes in the delight of poetry and learning. (True/False)
questions.explanation: काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन = in the delight of poetry and shastra; कालः गच्छति = time passes; धीमताम् = of the wise.

questions.question: Complete the line: 'तेजसां हि न ____ समीक्ष्यते।'
questions.explanation: तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते — of the brilliant, AGE is not considered.

questions.question: Complete the line: '____ हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते।'
questions.explanation: तेजसाम् (written तेजसां before हि) = 'of the brilliant ones', षष्ठी बहुवचन of तेजस्.

questions.question: रघुवंशम् इति महाकाव्यस्य कविः ____ अस्ति। (The poet of the Raghuvamsha is ____.)
questions.explanation: Kalidasa is the author of रघुवंशम्, the source of the chapter's title line.

questions.question: Complete the verse: 'न तेन वृद्धो भवति येनास्य ____ शिरः।'
questions.explanation: पलितं शिरः = a grey-haired head (पलितम् appears as पलितं before शिरः).

questions.question: Complete the verse: 'यो वै युवाप्यधीयानस्तं देवाः ____ विदुः।'
questions.explanation: The gods regard the learned youth as स्थविरम् — the elder.

questions.question: Complete the verse: 'काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति ____।'
questions.explanation: The time of THE WISE (धीमताम्) passes in the delight of poetry and learning.

questions.question: अष्टावक्रः ____ नृपस्य सभाम् अगच्छत्। (Ashtavakra went to the court of King ____.)
questions.explanation: He went to the court of Janaka (जनकस्य, षष्ठी 'of Janaka'), where he defeated Bandin.

questions.question: बालः रामः ____ नाम राक्षसीम् अवधीत्। (The boy Rama slew the demoness named ____.)
questions.explanation: Rama slew the demoness ताटका while protecting Vishvamitra's sacrifice.

questions.question: 'अध्वरः' इत्यस्य अर्थः ____ इति। (The meaning of 'adhvara' is ____.)
questions.explanation: अध्वरः is a synonym of यज्ञः, 'sacrifice'.

questions.question: 'क्षितीश्वरः' इत्यस्य अर्थः ____ इति। (The meaning of 'kshitishvara' is ____.)
questions.explanation: क्षिति (earth) + ईश्वरः (lord) = lord of the earth, i.e. राजा, the king.

questions.question: Complete Bhavabhuti's line: 'गुणाः ____ गुणिषु न च लिङ्गं न च वयः।'
questions.explanation: गुणाः पूजास्थानम् — qualities are the ground/place of honour.

questions.question: सन्धिं कुरुत: युवा + अपि = ____। (Join: yuva + api = ____.)
questions.explanation: आ + अ = आ (दीर्घ-सन्धिः): युवा + अपि = युवापि.

questions.question: सन्धिं कुरुत: च + एव = ____। (Join: cha + eva = ____.)
questions.explanation: अ + ए = ऐ (वृद्धि-सन्धिः): च + एव = चैव.

questions.question: 'तेजस्' शब्दस्य प्रथमा-बहुवचने रूपम् ____ अस्ति। (The nominative plural of 'tejas' is ____.)
questions.explanation: Neuter s-stem: तेजः (sg.) / तेजसी (dual) / तेजांसि (pl.).

questions.question: 'कौशिकेन' पदे ____ विभक्तिः अस्ति। (The vibhakti in 'Kaushikena' is ____.)
questions.explanation: कौशिकेन is instrumental (तृतीया) — 'BY Kaushika'.

questions.question: Describe the context of the verse 'कौशिकेन स किल क्षितीश्वरो...': who asked whom, and for what purpose?
questions.answer: The sage Vishvamitra (कौशिकः) approached King Dasharatha (क्षितीश्वरः) and asked him for his son Rama — then still a boy wearing the काकपक्ष side-locks — in order to quell the disruption that demons were causing to his sacrifice (अध्वरविघातशान्तये). The poet adds the reason the sage did not mind Rama's youth: तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते.
questions.explanation: Asker = Vishvamitra; asked = Dasharatha; object = the boy Rama; purpose = protection of the yajna.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'काकपक्षधरम्', and why is this word important in the verse?
questions.answer: काकपक्षधरम् = 'wearing the काकपक्ष', the crow's-wing side-locks of hair worn by boys. It is important because it stresses that Rama was still a mere child when the sage chose him for a dangerous task — making the point that age was not considered, only his तेजस्.
questions.explanation: The word paints Rama's boyhood and sharpens the contrast between his years and his task.

questions.question: Why did Dasharatha hesitate to send Rama with Vishvamitra, and what finally convinced him?
questions.answer: Dasharatha hesitated because Rama was still a young boy, and the demons disrupting the sacrifice were feared even by seasoned warriors. He was finally convinced by the counsel of the royal guru Vasishtha, who reminded him of Rama's extraordinary तेजस्; the king then sent Rama and Lakshmana with the sage.
questions.explanation: Hesitation = Rama's youth; persuasion = Vasishtha's word about Rama's brilliance.

questions.question: Write the meaning of: 'न तेन वृद्धो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः । यो वै युवाप्यधीयानस्तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः ॥'
questions.answer: One does not become old/venerable (वृद्धः) merely because his head has turned grey (पलितं शिरः). The one who, though young (युवा अपि), is devoted to study and learned (अधीयानः) — him the gods regard (विदुः) as the true elder (स्थविरः). Venerability comes from learning, not from years.
questions.explanation: The Manu verse: grey hair is no qualification; learning is.

questions.question: Quote Bhavabhuti's line on qualities and honour, name its source, and give its meaning.
questions.answer: The line is: 'गुणाः पूजास्थानं गुणिषु न च लिङ्गं न च वयः' — from Bhavabhuti's play उत्तररामचरितम्. Meaning: among the virtuous, qualities (गुणाः) alone are the ground of honour (पूजास्थानम्); neither outward form (लिङ्गम्) nor age (वयः) matters.
questions.explanation: Quote + source (उत्तररामचरितम्) + meaning: merit, not form or age, earns honour.

questions.question: Who was Ashtavakra, and why was he so named?
questions.answer: Ashtavakra was a brilliant boy sage of the Mahabharata (Vana Parva), son of Kahoda. He was called अष्टावक्रः because his body was bent (वक्र) in eight (अष्ट) places from birth. Though only about twelve, he defeated the great court scholar Bandin in debate at King Janaka's assembly.
questions.explanation: अष्ट + वक्र = bent in eight places; the boy sage of Janaka's court.

questions.question: What did Ashtavakra say to the courtiers who laughed at him, and what happened next?
questions.answer: When the courtiers laughed at his crooked body, Ashtavakra told them that they were looking only at the skin (चर्म) and not at knowledge (ज्ञानम्) — like judges of leather rather than judges of learning. He then debated the court scholar Bandin, defeated him, and thereby freed his father Kahoda, whom Bandin had earlier defeated.
questions.explanation: His retort exposes the error of judging by appearance; his victory proves merit over age.

questions.question: What deed of the young prince Raghu does Kalidasa describe in रघुवंशम् (sarga 3)?
questions.answer: Young Raghu, son of King Dilipa, was set to guard the horse of his father's अश्वमेध sacrifice. When Indra invisibly carried the horse away, the young prince pursued and fearlessly fought the king of the gods himself. Pleased by the boy's तेजस्, Indra granted Dilipa the fruit of the sacrifice.
questions.explanation: The episode shows a boy's courage matching a god — merit, not age.

questions.question: State two facts about the young Shankara (आदिशङ्कराचार्यः) mentioned in this chapter.
questions.answer: 1) By the age of eight he had mastered the four Vedas (अष्टवर्षे चतुर्वेदी), and by twelve all the shastras. 2) By sixteen he had composed his famous commentaries (भाष्य) on the Upanishads, the Gita and the Brahmasutra, and as a boy-sannyasi he travelled across India winning debates with the greatest scholars.
questions.explanation: Any two: Vedas at eight, all shastras at twelve, bhashyas at sixteen, victorious debates across India.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: तेजस्, वयः, याचितः, शान्तये, अध्वरः.
questions.answer: तेजस् = brilliance, inner fire, lustre; वयः = age; याचितः = was asked/begged; शान्तये = for the quelling/pacification; अध्वरः = sacrifice (यज्ञः).
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary of the मूलश्लोक.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: पलितम्, स्थविरः, अधीयानः, विदुः.
questions.answer: पलितम् = grey (of hair); स्थविरः = elder, venerable person; अधीयानः = one who is studying, learned; विदुः = (they) know, regard.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary of the Manu verse.

questions.question: From the हितोपदेश verse, give the meaning of: धीमताम्, व्यसनम्, निद्रा, कलहः.
questions.answer: धीमताम् = of the wise; व्यसनम् = vice, bad habit/addiction; निद्रा = sleep; कलहः = quarrel. The wise spend time in poetry and learning; fools in vice, sleep or quarrel.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary of काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम्...

questions.question: Explain the idea 'merit matters more than age' with one example from the chapter and one modern example of your own.
questions.answer: The chapter teaches that when real ability (तेजस्) is present, years should not be counted. Chapter example: Vishvamitra chose the boy Rama — still in his काकपक्ष side-locks — over grown warriors, and Rama slew Tataka and protected the sacrifice. Modern example (any suitable): a teenage chess grandmaster defeating senior players, a young scientist or coder creating an important invention, or a school student representing the country in sport — in each case selection by ability, not by age, is what the maxim recommends.
questions.explanation: One textual example (Rama/Ashtavakra/Raghu/Shankara) + one sensible modern parallel.

questions.question: Does 'तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते' teach disrespect toward elders? Give a reasoned answer.
questions.answer: No. The maxim does not lower elders; it only says that merit should not be denied because the meritorious person is young. The same tradition teaches विनयः (humility) and respect for elders. The right balance is to honour elders for experience and character, while also recognising and encouraging proven ability in the young.
questions.explanation: The maxim removes a false barrier (age) without removing respect.

questions.question: What error did Janaka's courtiers make in judging Ashtavakra, and what lesson does the episode give us for daily life?
questions.answer: The courtiers judged Ashtavakra by his outward appearance — his body bent in eight places and his young age — and laughed, assuming he could not be learned. Ashtavakra showed the error: they were seeing only skin (चर्म), not knowledge (ज्ञानम्). Lesson for daily life: never dismiss a person for looks, disability, age or dress; test ideas and ability, not appearances. Worth lives within.
questions.explanation: Error = judging by appearance/age; lesson = evaluate inner merit.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) and name the sandhi: (a) येनास्य (b) युवापि (c) चैव.
questions.answer: (a) येनास्य = येन + अस्य — दीर्घ-सन्धिः (अ + अ = आ). (b) युवापि = युवा + अपि — दीर्घ-सन्धिः (आ + अ = आ). (c) चैव = च + एव — वृद्धि-सन्धिः (अ + ए = ऐ).
questions.explanation: All three occur in the chapter's verses.

questions.question: Join with सन्धि: (a) याचितः + तेजसाम् (b) काकपक्षधरम् + एत्य.
questions.answer: (a) याचितः + तेजसाम् = याचितस्तेजसाम् (विसर्ग-सन्धिः: ः before त् becomes स्). (b) काकपक्षधरम् + एत्य = काकपक्षधरमेत्य (the final म् joins the following vowel ए).
questions.explanation: Both joins occur inside the मूलश्लोक itself.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति and the meaning-role of each word: कौशिकेन, रामम्, शान्तये, गुणिषु.
questions.answer: कौशिकेन = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'BY Kaushika'. रामम् = द्वितीया (accusative) → the object, '(asked for) Rama'. शान्तये = चतुर्थी (dative) → purpose, 'FOR the quelling'. गुणिषु = सप्तमी बहुवचन (locative plural) → 'AMONG the virtuous'.
questions.explanation: Four cases illustrated by four words of the chapter's verses.

questions.question: Write the प्रथमा forms (three numbers) of the neuter noun तेजस्, and explain the voice of the verb समीक्ष्यते.
questions.answer: तेजस् (neuter s-stem), प्रथमा: एकवचन तेजः, द्विवचन तेजसी, बहुवचन तेजांसि. समीक्ष्यते is कर्मवाचि (passive) of सम् + ईक्ष् 'to look at, consider': it means 'is considered', with वयः as its grammatical subject — 'age is not considered'.
questions.explanation: s-stem declension + passive voice recognition.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'एकदा महर्षिः विश्वामित्रः राजसभाम् आगच्छत्। सः अवदत् — हे राजन्! मम यज्ञं राक्षसाः विघ्नन्ति।'
questions.answer: Once the great sage Vishvamitra came to the royal court. He said — 'O king! Demons are disrupting my sacrifice.' (एकदा = once; राजसभाम् आगच्छत् = came to the royal assembly; अवदत् = said; विघ्नन्ति = obstruct/disrupt.)
questions.explanation: Simple narrative sentences from the chapter's Sanskrit story.

questions.question: Translate the full verse: 'कौशिकेन स किल क्षितीश्वरो राममध्वरविघातशान्तये । काकपक्षधरमेत्य याचितस्तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते ॥'
questions.answer: Kaushika (Vishvamitra), having approached, asked that king (Dasharatha) for Rama — a boy still wearing the side-locks of childhood — in order to quell the disruption of his sacrifice; for of the brilliant, age is not considered.
questions.explanation: कौशिकेन याचितः = was asked by Kaushika; अध्वरविघातशान्तये = for quelling the sacrifice's disruption; काकपक्षधरम् = the boy in side-locks.

questions.question: संस्कृतेन उत्तरत (Answer in Sanskrit): (a) कः रामं याचते? (b) रामः काम् अवधीत्?
questions.answer: (a) विश्वामित्रः (कौशिकः) रामं याचते। (b) रामः ताटकाम् अवधीत्।
questions.explanation: (a) Vishvamitra asks for Rama. (b) Rama slew Tataka.

questions.question: Explain the verse 'कौशिकेन स किल क्षितीश्वरो राममध्वरविघातशान्तये । काकपक्षधरमेत्य याचितस्तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते ॥' quarter by quarter, giving the शब्दार्थ of the key words and the full context.
questions.answer: Quarter 1 — कौशिकेन स किल क्षितीश्वरः: 'That lord of the earth (King Dasharatha), indeed, by Kaushika (Vishvamitra)...' — कौशिकेन is the agent (तृतीया); क्षितीश्वरः the king. Quarter 2 — राममध्वरविघातशान्तये: '...(was asked) for Rama, for the quelling of the disruption of his sacrifice' — अध्वरः = sacrifice, विघातः = disruption, शान्तये = for the quelling (चतुर्थी of purpose). Quarter 3 — काकपक्षधरमेत्य याचितः: 'having approached (एत्य), he was asked (याचितः) for the boy still wearing the काकपक्ष side-locks' — the word stresses Rama's childhood. Quarter 4 — तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते: 'for of the brilliant, age is not considered' — the poet's reason. Context: demons (Tataka, Maricha, Subahu) were disrupting Vishvamitra's yajna; he asked Dasharatha for the boy Rama; despite the king's hesitation, Rama went, slew Tataka and protected the sacrifice — proving that merit, not years, is the measure of a person.
questions.explanation: Expect quarter-by-quarter meaning, key शब्दार्थ (क्षितीश्वरः, अध्वरः, विघातः, शान्तये, काकपक्षधरः, याचितः), and the story context.

questions.question: Write any two supporting verses of this chapter (other than the title verse) with their sources, and explain how each supports the theme 'merit over age'.
questions.answer: 1) न तेन वृद्धो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः । यो वै युवाप्यधीयानस्तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः ॥ (मनुस्मृतिः) — Grey hair does not make one venerable; the learned youth is the true elder in the eyes of the gods. It directly says seniority belongs to learning, not to years. 2) गुणाः पूजास्थानं गुणिषु न च लिङ्गं न च वयः (भवभूतिः, उत्तररामचरितम्) — Among the virtuous, qualities alone are the ground of honour, not outward form nor age. It states as a general rule that honour follows गुण (merit). (Also acceptable: काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम्... from हितोपदेशः, showing that brilliance is built by spending time in study — so even the young can earn तेजस्.)
questions.explanation: Any two verses with source + a sentence linking each to the theme.

questions.question: Narrate the story of Ashtavakra at Janaka's court in detail — his birth-name's meaning, why he went to the court, how he was received, what he said, and how the episode ended. State the lesson of the story.
questions.answer: Ashtavakra (अष्ट + वक्र = 'bent in eight places') was born with a body crooked in eight places. His father Kahoda had been defeated in debate by Bandin, the court scholar of King Janaka, and detained under the debate's terms. Hearing this, the twelve-year-old Ashtavakra went to Janaka's court to challenge Bandin. The doorkeepers and courtiers, seeing a crooked young boy, burst out laughing. Ashtavakra rebuked them: 'You see only the skin (चर्म); you do not see knowledge (ज्ञानम्)' — they were judging like leather-workers, by the surface. Impressed, Janaka allowed the debate. The boy defeated Bandin with his learning and thereby freed his father Kahoda and the other defeated brahmanas. Lesson: wisdom is measured neither by the shape of the body nor by the number of years; judging by appearance or age is the mark of the shallow — तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते.
questions.explanation: Expect: name meaning, motive (father's defeat by Bandin), the courtiers' laughter, the skin-vs-knowledge retort, victory and the father's release, and the stated lesson.

questions.question: Break up and explain the meaning of these compound words from the chapter: (a) क्षितीश्वरः (b) काकपक्षधरः (c) अध्वरविघातशान्तये (d) काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन.
questions.answer: (a) क्षितीश्वरः = क्षिति (earth) + ईश्वरः (lord) → 'lord of the earth', the king (Dasharatha). (b) काकपक्षधरः = काकपक्ष (the 'crow's-wing' side-locks worn by boys) + धरः (wearing) → 'wearing the boyhood side-locks', i.e. still a child. (c) अध्वरविघातशान्तये = अध्वर (sacrifice) + विघात (disruption) + शान्तये (for the quelling, चतुर्थी) → 'for quelling the disruption of the sacrifice'. (d) काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन = काव्य (poetry) + शास्त्र (learning/science) + विनोदेन (in/by the delight, तृतीया) → 'in the delight of poetry and learning'.
questions.explanation: Each compound split into members with the case of the final member noted.

questions.question: Write a short essay: 'तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते in today's world.' Discuss what the maxim means, how society sometimes violates it, modern examples that prove it, and how it should be balanced with respect for elders.
questions.answer: Meaning: Kalidasa's line says that where true brilliance (तेजस्) exists, age should not be the measure. Violations: society often dismisses the young — 'you are too small to understand' — denying them opportunities in committees, decisions and leadership merely for their years; equally it may dismiss the old as 'outdated'. Both errors judge the calendar, not the person. Modern proofs: teenage grandmasters and Olympic medallists defeat seasoned champions; school students win national science awards; young programmers build products used by millions; India's own tradition offers Rama, Ashtavakra and Shankara as timeless examples. Institutions that select by demonstrated ability — auditions, olympiads, open competitions — embody the maxim. Balance: the maxim is not a licence for arrogance. The same shastra that honours the learned youth also demands विनयः (humility). Elders deserve respect for experience and sacrifice; the young deserve recognition for proven merit. A healthy family, school or nation honours both: it listens to grey hair and it gives wings to young fire. That is the complete teaching of तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते.
questions.explanation: Expect: meaning, social violations, 2-3 modern examples, and an explicit balance with respect for elders.

questions.question: Explain, with one example each from this chapter, the following sandhis: (a) दीर्घ-सन्धि (b) यण्-सन्धि (c) वृद्धि-सन्धि (d) विसर्ग-सन्धि.
questions.answer: (a) दीर्घ-सन्धि: a short/long simple vowel + a similar vowel merge into the long vowel — येन + अस्य = येनास्य (अ+अ=आ); also युवा + अपि = युवापि. (b) यण्-सन्धि: इ/ई, उ/ऊ, ऋ before a dissimilar vowel become य्, व्, र् — अपि + अधीयानः = अप्यधीयानः (इ+अ → य्), as inside युवाप्यधीयानः. (c) वृद्धि-सन्धि: अ/आ + ए/ऐ gives ऐ (and अ/आ + ओ/औ gives औ) — च + एव = चैव (अ+ए=ऐ). (d) विसर्ग-सन्धि: the visarga changes before certain consonants — याचितः + तेजसाम् = याचितस्तेजसाम् (ः before त् becomes स्).
questions.explanation: Definition + chapter example for each of the four sandhis.

questions.question: The words तेजस्, वयस्, शिरस् and मनस् are neuter s-stems. Write the प्रथमा forms (three numbers) of तेजस्, identify the forms तेजसाम्, वयः and शिरः as they occur in the chapter's verses, and explain what समीक्ष्यते tells us about the sentence structure of the title line.
questions.answer: प्रथमा of तेजस्: एकवचन तेजः, द्विवचन तेजसी, बहुवचन तेजांसि. In the verses: तेजसाम् is षष्ठी बहुवचन ('of the brilliant ones' — written तेजसां before हि); वयः is प्रथमा एकवचन of वयस् ('age'), the subject; शिरः is प्रथमा एकवचन of शिरस् ('head') in पलितं शिरः. समीक्ष्यते is a passive (कर्मवाचि) verb — so the title line is a passive sentence: वयः (subject, 'age') न समीक्ष्यते ('is not considered'), with तेजसाम् ('of the brilliant') as the genitive qualifier: 'of the brilliant, age is not considered'.
questions.explanation: Declension + identification of three s-stem forms + passive sentence analysis.

questions.question: (a) Translate into English the story passage: 'राजा अचिन्तयत् — रामः बालः अस्ति। कथं सः राक्षसान् जेष्यति? — इति। परन्तु गुरोः वसिष्ठस्य वचनेन सः रामं लक्ष्मणं च मुनये अयच्छत्।' (b) Then write three simple Sanskrit sentences of your own (in Devanagari) about any young achiever, with English meanings.
questions.answer: (a) Translation: The king thought — 'Rama is a boy. How will he conquer the demons?' But at the word of the guru Vasishtha he gave Rama and Lakshmana to the sage. (b) Sample sentences: 1. बालः शङ्करः वेदान् अपठत्। (The boy Shankara studied the Vedas.) 2. अष्टावक्रः वादे पण्डितम् अजयत्। (Ashtavakra defeated the scholar in debate.) 3. बाला अपि क्रीडायां देशस्य कीर्तिं वर्धयति। (Even a young girl increases the country's fame in sport.) Any three grammatically simple, meaningful sentences on a young achiever are acceptable.
questions.explanation: (a) tests comprehension of the story; (b) tests simple sentence composition with chapter vocabulary.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer the questions:
'कौशिकेन स किल क्षितीश्वरो राममध्वरविघातशान्तये ।
काकपक्षधरमेत्य याचितस्तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते ॥'
(a) Who is meant by कौशिकः and by क्षितीश्वरः?
(b) For what purpose was Rama asked for?
(c) What does the last quarter of the verse mean?
questions.answer: (a) कौशिकः = the sage Vishvamitra (born in Kushika's family); क्षितीश्वरः = the 'lord of the earth', King Dasharatha. (b) Rama was asked for in order to quell the disruption that demons were causing to the sage's sacrifice (अध्वरविघातशान्तये). (c) The last quarter — तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते — means 'for of the brilliant, age is not considered': the sage did not weigh Rama's years, only his तेजस्.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the मूलश्लोक: persons, purpose, and the maxim.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'राजा अचिन्तयत् — रामः बालः अस्ति। कथं सः राक्षसान् जेष्यति? — इति। परन्तु गुरोः वसिष्ठस्य वचनेन सः रामं लक्ष्मणं च मुनये अयच्छत्। बालः रामः ताटकां अवधीत्, मुनेः यज्ञं च अरक्षत्।'
(a) What was the king's doubt?
(b) On whose advice did he act?
(c) What did the boy Rama accomplish?
questions.answer: (a) The king doubted that Rama, being only a boy (बालः), could conquer the demons. (b) He acted on the advice (वचनेन) of the guru Vasishtha. (c) The boy Rama slew the demoness Tataka and protected the sage's sacrifice.
questions.explanation: Simple comprehension of the Sanskrit story passage.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
'न तेन वृद्धो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः ।
यो वै युवाप्यधीयानस्तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः ॥'
(a) According to the verse, what does NOT make a person venerable?
(b) Who is regarded by the gods as the true elder?
(c) Which word in the verse means 'studying/learned'?
questions.answer: (a) Mere grey hair (पलितं शिरः) — i.e. age by itself — does not make a person venerable. (b) The one who, though young (युवा अपि), is learned — him the gods regard as the elder (स्थविरः). (c) The word अधीयानः means 'studying/learned'.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the Manu verse and its key vocabulary.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'बालः अष्टावक्रः जनकस्य सभाम् अगच्छत्। सभासदः तस्य वक्रं शरीरं दृष्ट्वा अहसन्। बालः अवदत् — यूयं चर्म एव पश्यथ, ज्ञानं न पश्यथ — इति। ततः सः बन्दिनं वादे अजयत्, पितरं च अमोचयत्।'
(a) Why did the courtiers laugh?
(b) What did the boy tell them?
(c) What two things did he then achieve?
questions.answer: (a) The courtiers laughed on seeing the boy's crooked (वक्र) body. (b) He told them: 'You see only the skin (चर्म); you do not see knowledge (ज्ञानम्).' (c) He defeated Bandin in debate (वादे अजयत्) and freed his father (पितरम् अमोचयत्).
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the Ashtavakra passage: cause of laughter, the retort, the double achievement.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'In रघुवंशम् sarga 3, the young prince Raghu was set to guard the horse of his father Dilipa's ashvamedha sacrifice. When Indra invisibly carried the horse away, the boy pursued the king of the gods and fought him fearlessly. Pleased with his तेजस्, Indra granted the king the fruit of the sacrifice.'
(a) Whose sacrifice was it, and what was Raghu guarding?
(b) Who took the horse away?
(c) How does this episode illustrate the chapter's title?
questions.answer: (a) The अश्वमेध sacrifice was King Dilipa's; Raghu was guarding its sacrificial horse. (b) Indra, the king of the gods, carried it away invisibly. (c) Though only a young prince, Raghu fearlessly fought Indra himself, and Indra honoured his brilliance — showing that of the brilliant, age is not considered (तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते).
questions.explanation: The Raghu episode as a living example of the maxim.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
'काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम् ।
व्यसनेन च मूर्खाणां निद्रया कलहेन वा ॥'
(a) Give the meaning of काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन.
(b) Give the meaning of धीमताम् and मूर्खाणाम्.
(c) In one sentence, state the verse's message.
questions.answer: (a) काव्यशास्त्रविनोदेन = 'in the delight of poetry (काव्य) and learning (शास्त्र)'. (b) धीमताम् = 'of the wise'; मूर्खाणाम् = 'of the fools'. (c) Message: the wise spend their time in study and the arts, while fools waste it in vice, sleep and quarrel — so use time to build your तेजस्.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary and message of the हितोपदेश verse.

questions.question:
Read the situation and answer:
'A 14-year-old chess player qualifies for the state team. A senior member objects: she is too young to handle pressure — give the place to an older player. Her results, however, are the best in the state.'
(a) Which line of this chapter directly applies to the situation?
(b) What would Kalidasa's advice be, and why?
(c) How could the team also use the senior member's experience wisely?
questions.answer: (a) तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते — of the brilliant, age is not considered. (b) Kalidasa's advice: select the girl, because proven merit (best results), not age, is the right measure — just as Vishvamitra chose the boy Rama for a task grown warriors feared. (c) The senior's experience can still serve the team as a mentor, coach or strategist — respecting experience while giving the playing place to demonstrated ability.
questions.explanation: Application of the maxim to a modern selection dilemma, with the elder's role preserved.

questions.question:
Read the situation and answer:
'In a school committee, a Class 8 student suggests a simple water-saving idea. Some members dismiss it, saying juniors should not speak before seniors. The idea, when finally tested, saves thousands of litres.'
(a) What error did the members commit, in the light of this chapter?
(b) Which story of the chapter closely parallels this situation?
(c) State the correct principle in one Sanskrit line from the chapter.
questions.answer: (a) They judged the speaker's age instead of the idea's merit — exactly the error the chapter warns against. (b) Ashtavakra's story: the courtiers laughed at the boy's appearance and youth, yet his knowledge defeated the court's best scholar. (Vishvamitra's choice of the boy Rama is also a fair parallel.) (c) तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते (or गुणाः पूजास्थानं गुणिषु न च लिङ्गं न च वयः).
questions.explanation: Recognising the age-bias error, matching the parallel story, and citing the maxim.

questions.question:
Read the line and answer the grammar questions:
'तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते।'
(a) State the विभक्ति and वचन of तेजसाम्.
(b) Which word is the grammatical subject, and in which case is it?
(c) Is समीक्ष्यते active or passive? Give its meaning.
questions.answer: (a) तेजसाम् is षष्ठी विभक्ति, बहुवचन ('of the brilliant ones'). (b) The subject is वयः ('age'), in प्रथमा विभक्ति (एकवचन, neuter of वयस्). (c) समीक्ष्यते is passive (कर्मवाचि) — it means 'is considered/examined'; so the line reads 'of the brilliant, age is not considered'.
questions.explanation: Case analysis of the title line and recognition of the passive verb.

questions.question:
Read the Sanskrit passage and answer:
'बालः शङ्करः अष्टमे वर्षे चतुरः वेदान् अपठत्। षोडशे वर्षे सः भाष्याणि अरचयत्। सः भारतस्य सर्वासु दिक्षु अगच्छत्, पण्डितान् च वादे अजयत्।'
(a) Translate the passage into English.
(b) Which word means 'commentaries'?
(c) Which achievement mentioned here matches 'तेजसां हि न वयः समीक्ष्यते'?
questions.answer: (a) Translation: The boy Shankara studied the four Vedas in his eighth year. In his sixteenth year he composed the commentaries. He went to all the directions (corners) of India and defeated scholars in debate. (b) भाष्याणि means 'commentaries'. (c) All of them — mastering the Vedas at eight, writing भाष्यs at sixteen and defeating senior scholars in debate as a boy — show that brilliance, not age, is what counts.
questions.explanation: Translation of a simple prose passage about Shankara plus vocabulary and theme questions.
